brief: Convert the subtitle file episodes/ep-041-remote-work/subs/final.srt to WebVTT and save it next to it as final.vtt. Then split any cue longer than 42 characters per line into two lines at the nearest word boundary; never more than two lines per cue, and do not change any timestamps. Keep the original .srt untouched. Report the number of cues and how many you re-wrapped.

Rename the function `getUserCart` to `fetchCart` everywhere in the booking app repo (src/ and tests/ only). This covers the definition in src/cart/cartService.ts, all imports, all call sites, and the mocks in tests/__mocks__/cartService.ts. Don't touch anything else, and don't change behaviour. Run `npm run typecheck` once when you're done and paste the last 10 lines of its output. List the files you changed.

brand/northwind/palette.json has the client's colour tokens as nested JSON (group > token > {hex, rgb, usage}). Flatten it into brand/northwind/palette.csv with the columns group,token,hex,r,g,b,usage, one row per token, keeping the order from the JSON. Hex in uppercase with a leading #. Reply with nothing but the path and the row count.

I need a thorough, rigorous, line-by-line review of the last commit on branch chore/rename-theme-tokens before it merges into the production web app. Be exhaustive. The commit renames the CSS custom property `--color-primary-600` to `--brand-accent` across the stylesheets. Check that no occurrence of the old name is left anywhere in src/ or public/ (that includes .css, .scss, .tsx and inline style strings), that every new occurrence is spelled exactly the same, and that the commit changed nothing except the rename. Return PASS or FAIL, and for a FAIL list each stray occurrence as file:line.

Find where the feature flag `checkout_v2` is defined in the booking app (server config, the flag registry, env defaults, whichever applies) and list every place that reads it, on both server and client. For each read, give file:line and a one-line description of what the flag gates. Read only; change nothing. Under 300 words.

The nightly render runner left its logs in tools/render-runner/logs/ (about 40 files, one per job). Summarize them: how many jobs succeeded and how many failed, the distinct error messages grouped with a count for each, and which job ids took more than twice the median runtime. Don't try to fix anything. Return a short table and then three bullets on what looks worth investigating.

Look up on the web the current recommended upload specs for vertical short-form video on the three biggest short-video platforms: aspect ratio, max resolution, max length, the safe zones for captions and UI overlays, and the recommended bitrate if it's published. Use official help pages where they exist and cite a URL for every number. If two sources disagree, show both. Return a compact comparison table.

`legacyHttp()` in scripts/lib/net.py is deprecated. List every script under scripts/ and tools/ that still calls it, directly or through a wrapper. For each one: path:line, which arguments it passes (do any pass `verify=False` or a custom timeout?), and whether the script still looks alive (a cron entry in ops/crontab.txt, or a reference from the Makefile). Report only.

Review the diff in PR branch feat/partial-refunds against main, production booking app. The main changes are in src/billing/refund.ts and src/billing/webhooks/refundUpdated.ts, plus a new column in migrations/0087_refund_partial.sql. Focus on correctness with money: idempotency when the provider retries the webhook, rounding (we store minor units as integers), a partial refund that pushes the total refunded past the captured amount, and concurrent refund requests on the same booking. Also check that the ledger entries stay balanced. Give findings ranked by severity, each with file:line, a concrete failure scenario and a suggested fix. Don't edit the code.

Review src/server/middleware/session.ts as changed in the open PR (branch fix/session-sliding-expiry). It switches us from fixed to sliding session expiry and rotates the session id on privilege change. Check for session fixation, a rotation race when the same user has two tabs open, cookie flags, and whether logout really invalidates the server-side record. Return blocking issues first, then nits.

Small one, should be quick: review migrations/0091_add_tenant_id_to_bookings.sql and the matching model change in src/models/booking.ts. It adds `tenant_id NOT NULL` with a default and an index. The bookings table is our largest in production (tens of millions of rows) and the deploy runs migrations online. I want to know whether this locks the table, whether the backfill is safe, whether the index should be built concurrently, and what happens to app servers still running the old code during a rolling deploy. Verdict plus reasons.

Review the new rate limiter in src/server/rateLimit.ts and where it's wired in src/server/routes/auth.ts. It's a sliding window on the shared cache, keyed by IP plus email. Check that the window logic is right at the boundaries, how it behaves behind the load balancer (which header does it trust for the client IP?), what happens if the cache is down (fail open or fail closed, and is that the right call for login?), and whether an attacker can lock out a real user. Findings with file:line, under 400 words.

Quick look please: support says two customers occasionally end up booked into the same slot. It's rare, maybe a few times a week. The booking flow is src/bookings/createBooking.ts → src/bookings/slotLock.ts → the reservations table. Find out why it happens and propose a fix. Reproduce it if you can with a local concurrent script (scratch files only, no commits). Report the root cause with evidence and the fix you'd make.

Since yesterday's deploy, payment webhooks from the provider fail signature verification about 30% of the time, and those bookings stay stuck in 'pending'. The handler is src/billing/webhooks/handler.ts; the verify helper is src/billing/verifySignature.ts. The deploy diff is in deploy-notes/last-release.diff, and it includes a body-parser middleware reorder in src/server/app.ts. The failed requests are in logs/webhooks-failed.jsonl (bodies redacted, headers kept). Find the root cause, explain why it's only some of the requests, and give the minimal fix plus a safe way to replay the stuck events. Don't run anything against production.

Production API pods are getting OOM-killed a few times a day. The heap snapshots we grabbed point to the image upload route, src/server/routes/uploads.ts, which uses the resize pipeline in src/media/resize.ts. Crash logs are in incidents/oom/. Work out what is holding memory (buffering whole files? streams not destroyed on client abort? a cache with no bound?), confirm it with a local load test if possible, and propose a fix. Return the root cause, the evidence, and a patch as a diff in your reply; don't apply it.

Some users see their booking on the confirmation page one day earlier than the date they picked. It seems to be users west of UTC who book late in the evening. Trace the date from the picker (src/client/components/DatePicker.tsx) through the API (src/bookings/createBooking.ts) to storage and back out to the confirmation email template (templates/email/confirmation.mjml). Find every place the date gets converted, say which one is wrong, and suggest the fix. Also say whether bookings already stored are corrupted or only displayed wrong.

Review tools/deck-export/export.py. It's our internal script that turns the slide markdown into PDF and PNG thumbnails for the team; it doesn't ship to customers. Look for bugs, error handling that hides failures, and anything that would break on Windows paths. Keep it practical: the top 5 issues with line numbers and a fix for each, no style nitpicks.

The internal backup script scripts/backup_assets.sh silently skips files whose names contain spaces or brackets. Maya noticed missing renders in last night's archive. Find why (most likely word splitting in the find/loop or in the rsync args), fix it in place, and test it on a scratch folder with nasty filenames that you create in the scratchpad. Report what was wrong, the diff, and the test output.

Write a 'Local development' section for the booking app's README.md, to go right after the existing 'Overview' section. Base it on what is really in the repo (package.json scripts, docker-compose.yml, .env.example, scripts/seed.ts), not on assumptions. Cover prerequisites, first-time setup, seeding test data, running the tests, and the three most common setup errors (the troubleshooting notes are in docs/onboarding-notes.md). Match the tone of the existing README. Edit the file directly, then reply with a short summary.

Write speaker notes for the Larkspur brand pitch deck in brand/larkspur/pitch/deck.md. There are 14 slides; each one already has a title and bullets. For each slide, add a `Notes:` block of 60-120 words: what to say, the one point to land, and the hand-off to the next slide. The voice is warm and confident with no jargon. Base it on the strategy doc brand/larkspur/strategy.md; don't invent claims or numbers that aren't there. Edit deck.md in place.

Tidy up the shot list spreadsheet episodes/ep-042-city-gardens/shotlist.xlsx. Normalize the column headers (Scene, Shot, Description, Lens, Duration_s, Location, Status), turn durations written like '1m10' or '70 sec' into seconds, merge the duplicate rows (same scene+shot, keep the most complete one), sort by scene and then by shot, and freeze the header row. Save it as shotlist.clean.xlsx and leave the original alone. Report what you changed and flag any rows you couldn't resolve.

We need a background job queue for the booking app (Node/TypeScript, Postgres, Redis already in the stack). Compare the three candidates listed in docs/adr/draft-job-queue.md on: delivery guarantees, retries/backoff, scheduled and cron jobs, observability/dashboard, maintenance activity, and the operational cost of running it. Read their docs and the open issues on the points that matter. Write a finished recommendation into that ADR file, filling in its 'Options' and 'Decision' sections, with your reasoning and the risks.

Should our web app keep server-side session cookies or move to short-lived access tokens with refresh tokens, now that the mobile app is coming? Read several solid sources: the current OWASP guidance, a couple of well-regarded engineering write-ups, and the relevant RFCs. Weigh them against our setup, which is described in docs/architecture/auth.md. Deliver a finished 1-2 page recommendation in docs/research/session-vs-tokens.md covering the decision, the trade-offs, a migration path, and cited sources.

Deep investigation: transactional emails (booking confirmations, password resets) are landing in spam for a growing share of users, worst on the two biggest consumer mailbox providers. Pull together everything: our DNS records (dig the SPF, DKIM and DMARC for the sending domain in config/email.yml), the bounce and complaint exports in data/email/, the sending provider's docs, the mailbox providers' current published sender requirements, and the template changes in templates/email/ over the recent commits. Find the most likely causes, rank them by evidence, and write a remediation plan in docs/research/deliverability.md with sources. Don't change DNS or the provider settings.

Add unit tests for `formatMoney` in src/lib/money.ts. Don't change the function itself. Cover: zero, negative amounts, currencies with 0 and 3 minor units, large values, locale switching (en, de, fr) and an unknown currency code. Put them in tests/lib/money.test.ts using the existing vitest setup. If a test shows a real bug, leave that test marked `.fails` with a comment and tell me about it. Run the file and paste the result.

Add an optional `sort` query param to GET /api/bookings (src/server/routes/bookings.ts). Allowed values: `created_asc`, `created_desc` (the default, and today's behaviour) and `start_asc`. Anything else returns 400 with the existing error shape from src/server/errors.ts. Push the ordering down into the query in src/bookings/repo.ts; don't sort in memory. Add route tests next to the existing ones. Nothing else in scope.

Bug in the internal subtitle splitter tools/subsplit/split.py: when the input ends without a trailing blank line, the last cue gets dropped. Fix that specific bug, add a regression test in tools/subsplit/test_split.py, and run the tests. Keep the diff minimal.

Add a `--dry-run` flag to scripts/asset_sync.py. With the flag set, the script prints every upload and delete it would do (one line per action, prefixed DRY) and makes no network calls that write. Make sure the delete path is covered too, not just uploads. Follow the argparse style already in the file and add a test in scripts/tests/test_asset_sync.py that mocks the client and asserts no write methods get called. Report the diff summary and the test output.

Run the unit tests for the billing package only: `pnpm vitest run src/billing`. Don't fix anything. Return the pass/fail count and, for each failing test, the file, the test name and the first line of the assertion error. If the run crashes before any test executes, return the last 20 lines of output instead.

Write a README for tools/export-csv/ (a small Python CLI that dumps the orders table to CSV in batches). Read export.py and config.example.toml first. Cover: what it does, install (uv), the three flags (--since, --batch-size, --out), the env vars it reads, and one example run. Keep it under 80 lines, plain Markdown, no badges. Write it to tools/export-csv/README.md and return the file path plus anything in the code you found confusing or undocumented.

Second attempt — the previous run produced a migration that dropped the old column in the same step and would have lost data on rollback. Do it in two phases this time.

Task: split `customers.full_name` into `first_name` and `last_name` in the Postgres schema (migrations live in db/migrations/, Drizzle schema in src/db/schema/customers.ts).
Phase 1 migration: add the two nullable columns, backfill from full_name (split on the last space; single-word names go to first_name, last_name stays NULL), keep full_name untouched. Update the schema file and every read/write site so new writes fill all three columns. Grep for `fullName` and `full_name` across src/ and the admin API in src/api/admin/.
Do NOT write phase 2 (dropping full_name) — just leave a TODO note in the migration file header.
Run `pnpm db:check` and `pnpm vitest run src/customers` and include the output. Return: the migration file name, the list of files you changed with a one-line reason each, and any call site you weren't sure about.

Check the exported logo pack for Northwind Coffee in brandbook/exports/logo-pack/. Against brandbook/specs/logo-spec.md verify: every variant listed in the spec exists in SVG, PNG@1x and PNG@2x; PNG sizes match the spec table; file names follow `nw-logo-<variant>-<color>.<ext>`; the reversed variants have transparent backgrounds. You only check files — another agent is already checking colour values, so skip hex codes. Return a short list: missing files, wrong sizes, bad names, non-transparent backgrounds. Write "clean" if nothing is wrong.

Write the final voiceover script for episode 12 of the explainer series ("Why your phone battery dies faster in winter"). Inputs: episodes/ep12/outline.md (approved beat list, 9 beats), episodes/ep12/research-notes.md (facts with sources — use only these, invent no numbers), and style/voice-guide.md (host persona, banned phrases, reading level).
Target 3:30–3:50 spoken at 150 wpm. Open with the cold-hook from beat 1 exactly as approved; end on the call to action from the guide. Every factual line must trace to a note — mark it inline as [n3], [n7] etc., the editor strips them later. No jokes about specific phone brands.
This goes straight to the narrator after a light edit, so it must read aloud cleanly: short sentences, no parentheses, numbers written as spoken. Save to episodes/ep12/vo-script.v1.md and return the word count, estimated runtime, and any beat where the notes felt too thin to support the line.
run tests
lint fix
Summarize what changed on this branch vs main in 5 bullets.
Why does scripts/sync-assets.sh exit 0 when rsync fails?

Find where the booking app sends the confirmation email after a reservation is made. I need the file and function that builds the email payload and the place it's queued. Return paths with line numbers, nothing else.

Search clients/fernhill/ for every deck and doc that still uses the old tagline "Grown for good" (any casing, also split across lines in .md and in speaker notes of the exported .pptx XML under decks/_unzipped/). Other agents are covering the website copy and social folders, so skip site/ and social/. Return file path, line or slide number, and the surrounding sentence for each hit.

Find out how refunds can end up issued twice. Support reports a handful of customers refunded double for one cancelled order in the last week. Trace the full refund path in production code: the admin "Refund" action (src/api/admin/orders/refund.ts), the payment-provider webhook handler (src/webhooks/payments.ts), and the nightly reconciliation job (src/jobs/reconcile-refunds.ts). For each, note where a refund record is created, what idempotency key (if any) is sent to the provider, whether there's a DB lock or unique constraint guarding it (check db/migrations/ for constraints on refunds), and how retries are handled. Look specifically for a race between the webhook and the reconciliation job, and for the admin button being clickable twice. Read-only — do not change anything. Return: the most likely cause with file:line evidence, any other plausible paths ranked, and what you could not confirm from code alone.
